text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Tuesday:

- Some 18,000 people sought asylum in Switzerland during 1996, a total of 980 or 5.8 percent more than in the previous year. More than one-third of those came from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia (Serbia, Kosovo and Montenegro), according to government statistics.

- The number of unemployed in the Swiss building sector rose to 3,456, or 18.7 percent of the workforce, in December. Every third person now applying for unemployment benefits is from construction industries.
- Basle-based pharmaceuticals group Roche obtained European marketing rights to VIRACEPT, an anti-HIV medication developed by Agouron and Japan Tobacco Inc.
- The Swiss Economic Institute KOF expects unemployment to rise to 6.7 percent by 1998 from the current 5.3 percent.

- The number of people hit by long-term joblessness in Switzerland rose by 6.8 percent to more than 52,375 from November to December. Nearly 28 percent of all unemployed in Switzerland have been without a job for more than a year.
- Mitropa AG, a subsidiary of German Railways, will take over the core business of Buffet Suisse from March 1.
- New pharmaceuticals giant Novartis named Wayne P. Yetter new CEO of its U.S. pharmaceutical operations.
